title: Shopify Plus vs Adobe Commerce: 2026 Comparison for APAC
summary: A Shopify Plus Adobe Commerce comparison for 2026 from an APAC operator's view: real cost drivers, B2B depth, replatforming triggers and a decision framework.
body_markdown:
**Quick Answer:** In 2026, Shopify Plus wins on total cost of operation for most APAC retailers because infrastructure, patching and scaling are vendor-owned. Adobe Commerce still wins where commercial logic is genuinely proprietary — configurable products, contract pricing, multi-entity B2B — and you fund a permanent engineering team.


---


# Shopify Plus vs Adobe Commerce: The 2026 Comparison Guide


The Shopify Plus Adobe Commerce comparison in 2026 is no longer a feature fight. Both platforms will render a product page, take a payment, and sync an order to your ERP. The real decision is about who carries the operational load — your team, or the vendor — and what that costs you over three years in a region where you may be running six countries, four currencies, and two fulfilment models from one commerce stack.


*Related reading:*[Shopify Plus vs Adobe Commerce B2B Asia: 2026 Verdict](https://branch8.com/posts/shopify-plus-vs-adobe-commerce-b2b-asia)


*Related reading:*[AI Spending and Infrastructure Cost Optimization in APAC for 2026](https://branch8.com/posts/ai-spending-infrastructure-cost-optimization-apac)


My bias, stated up front: for the majority of Asia-Pacific mid-market and enterprise retailers we assess, Shopify Plus wins on total cost of operation. Not licence cost — operation. The exceptions are real and I'll name them. But the default has flipped since 2024, and the migration traffic across the region is running one direction. This Shopify Plus Adobe Commerce comparison lays out exactly where and why.


## The verdict in 60 seconds


**Choose Shopify Plus if** your commercial model is recognisably retail — B2C, DTC, wholesale-with-price-lists, multi-market storefronts — and your competitive advantage is merchandising speed rather than proprietary commerce logic. You will spend less on infrastructure, less on upgrade cycles, and you will ship campaigns faster.


**Choose Adobe Commerce if** your catalogue, pricing, or entitlement logic is genuinely non-standard — configurable industrial products with rule-driven pricing, dealer networks with per-account contract terms, multi-entity B2B where each buyer sees a different catalogue — and you have (or will fund) a permanent engineering team. Adobe's flexibility is real. It is also a standing cost line.


**Choose neither** if you are a single-market SEA or Greater China brand where social commerce, live selling, and WhatsApp/LINE ordering drive the majority of revenue. SHOPLINE and regional platforms handle those channels natively, according to SHOPLINE's 2025 regional commerce report; you will bolt them onto Shopify or Adobe at real expense.


## What actually changed between 2024 and 2026


If you last ran this evaluation two years ago, three things have moved enough to invalidate your notes.


**Adobe went SaaS-first.** Adobe launched Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service and Adobe Commerce Optimizer in 2025, per Adobe's own product announcements — a SaaS, API-first deployment that decouples the storefront and catalogue services from the monolithic PHP application. This is a genuine strategic response to Shopify. It also means the Adobe Commerce you evaluate in 2026 is not the Adobe Commerce your team learned in 2019, and the Magento Open Source lineage is increasingly a separate track from the commercial roadmap. Adobe's own documentation now distinguishes between the Cloud Service, the Managed Services PaaS, and the on-premise edition — three products with different upgrade paths.


**Shopify got serious about enterprise B2B and composability.** Shopify B2B is now native to Plus rather than a Handshake-era bolt-on: company accounts, per-company catalogues and price lists, payment terms, and net-30 invoicing ship in the platform. Hydrogen and Oxygen give you a headless React storefront hosted by Shopify at no additional hosting line, and Shopify Functions replaced most of the old script-editor and app-based customisation surface for discounts, shipping, and payment logic, according to Shopify's 2025 B2B and developer platform documentation.


**Pricing converged at the entry point and diverged at the total.** Shopify Plus starts at USD 2,300 per month on a three-year term, per Shopify's published Plus pricing, moving to variable rates above roughly USD 800,000 monthly GMV. Adobe Commerce does not publish list pricing; Adobe quotes on GMV bands, and mid-market APAC quotes typically land in a comparable annual range once Cloud infrastructure is included. The licence line is not where these platforms differ. The engineering line is.

## The seven-dimension comparison framework


Run both platforms through the same seven questions. Score them for *your* business, not in the abstract.


### 1. Total cost of operation, not licence cost


Shopify commissioned Forrester Consulting research claiming a 29% lower total cost of ownership versus Adobe Commerce, according to Forrester's 2025 Total Economic Impact study published on Shopify's enterprise site. Treat vendor-commissioned TEI studies with the scepticism they deserve — but the mechanism behind the number is sound and you can verify it against your own budget.


On Adobe Commerce you pay for: licence, cloud infrastructure (Adobe Commerce on Cloud runs on AWS/Azure with Fastly CDN), a systems integrator or in-house team, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch operations, PHP version upgrades, quarterly security patch application, and extension licence renewals. On Shopify Plus you pay for: licence, transaction/payment fees, apps, and a partner or in-house team for storefront and integration work. Infrastructure, patching, PCI scope, and Black Friday scaling are Shopify's problem.


The honest counter-argument: Shopify's payment processing economics matter at scale. If you don't use Shopify Payments, Shopify charges a third-party gateway fee. In markets where Shopify Payments isn't available — and coverage across Southeast Asia is uneven — that fee is a real line item that Adobe doesn't have. Model it at your actual GMV before you conclude anything.


### 2. Time to change something


This is the metric most evaluations skip and most CFOs care about six months post-launch. How long from "marketing wants a new bundle promotion in Australia only" to it being live?


On Shopify Plus, a discount rule that can't be expressed in the native discount engine goes into a Shopify Function — deployed independently, no store downtime:


```text
1  shopify app generate extension --template product_discount    2  shopify app deploy
```


The Function itself is Rust or JavaScript compiled to WASM, running inside Shopify's checkout with a hard execution budget. Constrained, but predictable.


On Adobe Commerce the equivalent is a module, a deployment pipeline, and a full-cache invalidation:


```text
1  bin/magento module:enable Vendor_CustomPricing    2  bin/magento setup:upgrade    3  bin/magento setup:di:compile    4  bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy en_AU en_SG    5  bin/magento cache:flush
```


Anyone who has run` setup:di:compile` on a large catalogue during a release window knows what that costs in calendar time. Adobe's Cloud Service deployment reduces this materially — but only for merchants on the new SaaS track, not for the large installed base on 2.4.x PaaS.


### 3. Multi-country and multi-currency operations


For APAC operators this is usually the deciding dimension. Shopify Markets handles per-market pricing, currency, domains, and duties-inclusive pricing from a single store, with Markets Pro extending merchant-of-record coverage in supported regions. Adobe Commerce handles multi-store natively through website/store/store-view scoping — architecturally more flexible, operationally heavier, because every scope multiplies your configuration and content surface.


Rule of thumb from replatforming assessments: if your markets share a catalogue and differ mainly by price, language, and payment method, Shopify Markets is faster. If your markets have genuinely different catalogues, legal entities, tax logic, and warehouse ownership — a Japan business that shares almost nothing with your Australia business — Adobe's scoping model earns its complexity.


### 4. B2B and dealer-network depth


Adobe still leads here, and it's not close on the hardest cases. Per-customer-group catalogues, negotiated quote workflows, requisition lists, purchase-order approval hierarchies, and complex tier pricing are first-class in Adobe Commerce B2B.


Shopify B2B has closed most of the gap for the common cases: company accounts with multiple locations, per-company price lists, payment terms, and draft-order quoting. Where it still strains is multi-level approval chains and pricing that depends on runtime calculation against contract terms held in an external system.


A pattern we see repeatedly with manufacturers selling through dealer networks in Greater China and ANZ, and consistent with findings in Gartner's 2025 digital commerce vendor analysis: the pricing logic doesn't actually belong in the commerce platform at all. It belongs in the ERP or a pricing service, exposed over an API, with the storefront rendering the answer. Once you accept that architecture, the Adobe advantage shrinks considerably — because you're no longer asking the platform to be the system of record for commercial terms.


### 5. Performance and Core Web Vitals


Shopify Plus ships fast by default because the hosting, CDN, and image pipeline are not your decision. Adobe Commerce can be made equally fast — Adobe's own Edge Delivery Services and the Fastly integration exist for exactly this — but "can be made" is doing heavy lifting. Out of the box, a stock Adobe Commerce install with a full-featured theme and a dozen extensions will not match a stock Shopify Plus theme on Largest Contentful Paint.


Google's Core Web Vitals thresholds (LCP under 2.5s, INP under 200ms, CLS under 0.1, per web.dev) are the benchmark that matters. Both platforms can hit them. Only one hits them without you funding a performance workstream.


### 6. Ecosystem depth and integration reality


The Shopify App Store lists over 13,000 apps according to Shopify's own developer documentation — enormous breadth, variable quality, and a dependency risk: an app that goes unmaintained is your problem. Adobe Commerce Marketplace is smaller but the extensions tend to be deeper and, critically, you can fork them because you have the code, according to Adobe's 2025 Commerce Marketplace documentation.


For APAC-specific integrations, check three things before you commit: local payment methods (FPS in Hong Kong, PayNow in Singapore, DuitNow in Malaysia, QRIS in Indonesia), local logistics (SF Express, Ninja Van, J&T), and your accounting or ERP stack. Coverage on both platforms is decent for the majors and thin for the long tail. Budget for at least one custom integration you didn't plan for.


### 7. Talent availability across the region


This one is chronically under-weighted. Certified Adobe Commerce backend engineers in Hong Kong, Singapore, and Sydney are scarce and expensive, and the supply is not growing — the developer talent pipeline has been flowing toward JavaScript and SaaS platforms for years, a trend also flagged in Gartner's 2025 digital commerce vendor analysis and echoed in a 2025 LinkedIn Asia-Pacific talent report. Shopify's development surface (Liquid, React/Remix, GraphQL Admin API) draws from a far larger pool, including strong teams in Vietnam, the Philippines, and Malaysia.


If your platform choice depends on hiring three PHP specialists in a market where they don't exist, you have chosen a risk, not a platform.


## The APAC replatforming pattern nobody puts in the sales deck


The direction of travel across the region is documented. MR DIY Malaysia's migration from Magento to Shopify Plus is published as a case study on Shopify's own enterprise site — a large-format home improvement retailer moving off a self-managed Magento estate onto SaaS commerce, with the stated drivers being operational efficiency and cost of ownership rather than any missing storefront feature. Read it with the appropriate discount for it being a vendor case study, but the shape of the story matches what we see in assessment after assessment.


The pattern goes like this. A retailer implemented Magento 1 or early Magento 2 between 2016 and 2020, when it was the sensible enterprise choice. The build was customised heavily. Then the upgrade tax arrived: Magento 1 end-of-life in June 2020 (per Adobe's published lifecycle policy), the 2.4 upgrade, PHP 8.x requirements, Elasticsearch version bumps, and a security patch cadence that requires a standing team just to stay current. Meanwhile the extensions that made the original build viable stopped being maintained.


By year five, the retailer is spending most of its commerce engineering budget on staying still. That's the replatforming trigger — not features.


The honest counterweight: replatforming is expensive and disruptive. Data migration, URL and SEO preservation, re-integration of every downstream system, and retraining the merchandising team are all real costs, and they land in one financial year. A migration that saves 30% annually against a build that took eighteen months and blew its budget is not a win. If your Adobe estate is current, patched, and your team is comfortable — staying is a defensible decision. Migrate on a trigger, not on a trend.

## When to choose Shopify Plus


Pick Shopify Plus when most of these are true:


- Your revenue is predominantly B2C, DTC, or straightforward wholesale.
- You operate across multiple APAC markets that share a catalogue and differ by price, language, and payment method.
- Your merchandising and campaign cadence is weekly or faster, and speed-to-market is a commercial advantage.
- You do not want to own infrastructure, PCI scope, or patch cycles.
- Your peak traffic is spiky — 11.11, 12.12, Chinese New Year, Black Friday — and you'd rather not capacity-plan for it.
- Your integration needs are covered by established connectors plus one or two custom builds.
- You want a headless storefront but not a headless hosting bill: Hydrogen on Oxygen is included with Plus.


The trade-off you are accepting: checkout customisation is bounded by what Shopify Functions and Checkout Extensibility allow, you don't own the code that runs your platform, and app dependency is a real operational risk.


## When to choose Adobe Commerce


Pick Adobe Commerce when most of these are true:


- Your commercial logic is the product — configurable manufacturing, rule-driven contract pricing, per-account entitlements that can't be expressed as price lists.
- You run multiple legal entities with genuinely divergent catalogues, tax treatment, and fulfilment across markets.
- You have B2B approval workflows with multiple levels and requisition management.
- You already run Adobe Experience Manager, Adobe Analytics, or Real-Time CDP, and the integration value is material.
- You have a funded, permanent engineering team — not a project team, a permanent one.
- Data residency or regulatory constraints require deployment control that SaaS won't give you.


The trade-off: you own the upgrade path, the security posture, the performance budget, and the hiring problem. Adobe's move to the Cloud Service reduces some of that for new implementations, but it's a newer product with a shorter production track record than the PaaS it's replacing.

## Why is Shopify Plus so expensive — and is it still worth it in 2026?


The two questions people actually search for, answered plainly.


Shopify Plus costs what it costs because you are buying an operations department, not software. USD 2,300 monthly on a three-year term (Shopify's published pricing) buys hosting at Black Friday scale, PCI DSS Level 1 compliance, uptime, patching, the checkout — which Shopify does not let you break — and a support tier with a merchant success manager. Priced against one mid-level DevOps engineer in Singapore or Sydney, the licence is not the expensive part of your commerce stack.


Is it worth it in 2026? For most retailers, yes — with a caveat. Shopify keeps extending its share of hosted commerce, and its GMV growth has continued to outpace overall e-commerce market growth in recent quarters per Shopify's published quarterly results. That momentum funds the roadmap you're buying into. The caveat is your payment mix: if you can't use Shopify Payments in your primary markets, run the third-party gateway fee against your actual volume before signing. At high GMV with external processing, the arithmetic can genuinely favour Adobe.


And Shopify's biggest competitor? In the enterprise segment it's Adobe Commerce and Salesforce Commerce Cloud. In APAC specifically it's neither — it's SHOPLINE in Greater China and Southeast Asia, and the marketplaces themselves. A brand doing most of its volume on Shopee, Lazada, Tmall, or Douyin is making a channel decision, not a platform decision.


## Your decision framework


Skip the feature matrix. Answer five questions in order, and stop at the first one that gives you a clear answer.


**1. Is your commercial logic standard or proprietary?** Write down the three most complex pricing or entitlement rules in your business. If a Shopify B2B price list plus a Shopify Function can express all three, Adobe's flexibility is a cost with no return. If any of them requires runtime calculation against contract state, either move that logic to a service or choose Adobe.


**2. What is your permanent engineering headcount, funded for three years?** Under three engineers dedicated to commerce, Adobe Commerce on the PaaS track will consume all of them on maintenance. Be honest — count the people you actually have, not the ones in the org chart proposal.


**3. What is your true multi-market structure?** Shared catalogue with local pricing points to Shopify Markets. Separate entities, catalogues, and tax logic per country points to Adobe scoping — or to more than one Shopify store, which is a legitimate answer people dismiss too quickly.


**4. What does your payment mix cost on each platform?** Model three years at projected GMV. Shopify Payments availability by market, third-party gateway fees, and Adobe's gateway-agnostic position. This single calculation reverses the TCO conclusion often enough that it must be done with real numbers.


**5. What triggers change?** If your current platform is current, patched, and your team ships comfortably, do nothing. Replatform on a trigger — end-of-life, an upgrade you can't fund, a market expansion the platform can't serve, a security posture you can't defend. Not on a comparison article, including this one.


Work through those five and the Shopify Plus Adobe Commerce comparison stops being a debate and becomes arithmetic.
